name: Principal-Ordinates Propagation
definition: A deterministic finite-element scheme for real-time simulation of anisotropic light transport in heterogeneous participating media. It solves the problem of false scattering and ray effects inherent in previous finite-element methods by dynamically decomposing illumination into directional and point sources and propagating them in independent discrete domains aligned with principal light directions.
summary: Principal-Ordinates Propagation is a deterministic finite-element method for real-time anisotropic light transport that eliminates false scattering by using a unimodal basis aligned with principal directions.
